label: first input token is c
explanation: Fires at step 0 when the first original token is the letter c, at a near-constant magnitude of about 1.15 (the max), with no dependence on L or later tokens. That accounts for 99.8% of activation mass. The only other firing is a weak activation (~0.07) when c is input at step 1 right after a first token k ("k c ..."), plus 7 tiny activations in the copy phase when c is output/input there. It does not fire on c anywhere else in the original sequence, on the delimiter, or during copying in general.

issues: Every claim checks out. On test, the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.971, F1 0.985 and mass recall 0.998, with zero false positives. In the profile, t=0 holds 0.998 of the mass and the median magnitude is 1.152, which equals the max; the mean is 1.116 because of the small activations. There are no firings on the delimiter and no firings for any input token other than c.

The misses are not random noise. All 510 test misses are c at step 1 right after a first token k (about 0.06 of max). The explanation already reports this case and its mass is only 0.2%, so it does not refute the label.

The 7 copy-phase firings (5 on test) are also a pattern. They occur in L=3 sequences that start with c (activation 0.05-0.12 of max) and fall at step 4, the first input after <DEL>, where the model feeds back its own output c. The explanation calls them 'near-zero', which is accurate. It is a slight oversimplification to say they are not tied to copying, but their mass is about 0.
